lede: The most consequential thing happening this week isn't a concert or a cookout — it's a quiet worksession at the Telluride Housing Authority Subcommittee on Wednesday, where staff will dig into whether the town's lending guidelines actually work for mixed-use housing structures, a question that directly affects who can buy into deed-restricted units here. Wednesday also brings the Board of County Commissioners, where a Planning Commission alternate seat gets filled and the Forest Service joins a conversation about high-country road access policy. Ouray County's Planning Commission is meanwhile reopening its Land Use Code definitions — the kind of foundational language that shapes every zoning call that follows.

notable.stake: Lending rule changes could expand or restrict who qualifies for local deed-restricted housing.
Planning Commission seat filled; road access policy with Forest Service could set precedent.
Land use definition changes shape what triggers county review for years to come.
